# Reference Case D — Audit reconstruction

**Codokey Reference Cases v1.0.0 · validator `tools/codokey-check.mjs`**

> Logs exist in most organizations; reconstruction often fails anyway because records are not linked by session, omit the delegating human, or never captured what the agent could read.

## Scenario

After a suspected exposure, an investigator must answer eight questions about an agent session: who acted, for whom, when, with what scope, with which secret paths readable, what changed, who approved, and who authorized deployment. Two event exports are compared.

## Assumptions

- Event format follows the Codokey Audit Evidence Specification v1.0 (kit/audit-evidence-specification.md).
- Records with source "agent-self-report" are treated as writable by the agent and fail the tamper-protection check.

## Synthetic inputs

- events.complete.jsonl — eight correlated events from platform audit log and agent session log
- events.incomplete.jsonl — missing delegation, scope, end event, a session-less approval, and agent self-reported records

All values are synthetic. No real credentials, repositories, or systems are used.

## Protocol layers

06 Audit Memory, 01 Code Origin, 02 Key Exposure

## Control expectations

- Each event has the required fields (CK-AM-01).
- Each event links to a session (CK-AM-01).
- Q1–Q8 are answerable for every session (CK-AM-01, CK-OR-02).
- Records come from sources outside agent write access (CK-AM-02).

## Observable pass/fail conditions

| Check | Condition |
|---|---|
| D1 | FAIL if any event lacks a required field. |
| D2 | FAIL if any event lacks session_id. |
| D3 | FAIL if any reconstruction question cannot be answered for a session. |
| D4 | FAIL if any record is agent self-reported. |

## Evidence requirements (real-world equivalent)

An export of one real session's records (platform audit log + agent session log), with secret values removed, mapped to the specification fields.

## Reproduce

```sh
node tools/codokey-check.mjs audit-reconstruct --events cases/d-audit-reconstruct/events.complete.jsonl   # expect PASS
node tools/codokey-check.mjs audit-reconstruct --events cases/d-audit-reconstruct/events.incomplete.jsonl   # expect FAIL (D1, D2, D3, D4)
```

## Expected outcome

complete → PASS. incomplete → FAIL on D1, D2, D3, D4.

## Limitations

- Checks presence and linkage of fields, not their truthfulness.
- Many agent products do not currently export "readable_secret_paths"; the specification marks this field as frequently unavailable.
